newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN CALL MONEY RATES EDGE DOWN AFTER REPO NEWS.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN CALL MONEY RATES EDGE DOWN AFTER REPO NEWS.

text.p: German call money rates eased marginally on Tuesday after the Bundesbank set this week's repo tender at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent.
Call money rates were quoted in a range of 3.10 to 3.15 percent with the bulk of trades done at 3.125 percent, down from 3.15 percent on Monday.

Dealers predicted the Bundesbank will pump up to three billion marks in additional funds into the market in Wednesday's repo allocation to prevent a rise in call money rates as market liquidity remains tight.
The Bundesbank signalled unchanged monetary policy by calling for bids for repo funds at a fixed 3.00 percent.
Financial markets had speculated the bank might depart from its policy of setting fixed-rate repo tenders at that rate and allow the rate to drift higher to support the mark.

The mark has fallen sharply against the dollar and other European currencies this year. Money dealers said they were not surprised at the Bundesbank's decision and said speculation of a possible shift in monetary policy would now focus on the Bundesbank's next council meeting on August 21.
"I expect the repo rate will remain at three percent next week as well, but speculation may flare up again ahead of the next council meeting," one dealer said.
Analysts said the Bundesbank was keeping its options open by only announcing terms of the repo for this week and saying nothing about next week's tender.
But the bank is generally expected to wait at least until its August 21 meeting before deciding on any change.
Dealers said call money rates were being kept firm as a result of tight liquidity in the money market and predicted the rate could come down slightly after Wednesday's allocation.
Commercial banks' effective deposits rose to 39.7 billion marks on Monday from 37.6 billion on Friday.
The monthly average was unchanged at 39.7 billion marks. Banks' borrowings from the Bundesbank's Lombard facility were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was 3.14867 percent on Tuesday, down from 3.16600 percent on Monday.
